conventions.window: Browser window about 1440 × 900, zoom 100%, light theme
conventions.format: PNG. Crop to the area named in "Capture"; no browser chrome, no desktop.
conventions.naming: Save as <id>.png (the file name shown on each card).
conventions.data: Use the sample named on each card from the demo gallery; no personal or unpublished data.

shots.title: The viewer with regions and the Region Editor
shots.capture: Viewer area (toolbar + image + Region Editor), no demo gallery
steps: Open the demo and click the WSI tile 'CMU-1 · 1.5 Gpx (CC0)'.
Zoom in on a piece of tissue (scroll) until a few glands fill the view.
Draw 3–4 regions: two rectangles (r), one freeform (f), one wand region (w).
Open the Region Editor (Region Editor button) and give two regions the class 'Tumor' and one 'Stroma' in the Class column.
Capture the viewer area: toolbar, image with minimap and scale bar, and the Region Editor on the right.

shots.title: The viewer with img01.png just opened
shots.capture: Viewer area (toolbar + image + minimap), no demo gallery
steps: Open the live demo in a 1440×900 window.
Click the sample 'img01.png' in the gallery and wait until it is sharp.
Do not zoom or select any tool.
Capture the viewer area: toolbar on top, the full image, and the minimap at the bottom right.

shots.title: Minimap (bottom right) and scale bar (bottom left)
steps: Open the WSI 'CMU-1 · 1.5 Gpx (CC0)'.
Zoom in a few steps so the red view rectangle in the minimap is small.
Capture the viewer area; minimap bottom-right and the µm scale bar bottom-left must both be visible.

shots.title: Channels & Histogram on an RGB image
steps: Open 'img04.png'.
Click the Channels & Histogram button (half-filled drop icon).
Click the 'Green' row so the histogram shows Green.
Capture the dialog only.

shots.title: Heatmap plot type
steps: Open 'img01.png'.
Pick 'Heatmap' in the plot-type dropdown.
Capture the viewer area (Plotly heatmap with its colour bar).

shots.title: Volume plot type
steps: Load the micro-ct folder as a z-stack (right-click a slice).
Pick 'Volume'. Wait for 'Building … in 3D…' to finish.
Drag to rotate so the volume is seen at an angle; capture the viewer area, including the 3D toolbar controls.

shots.title: A rectangle and a freeform region, listed in the Region Editor
shots.capture: Viewer area including the Region Editor
steps: Open 'img01.png'.
Click 'Open the Region Editor' in the toolbar; leave it docked on the right.
Press r and drag a rectangle around one muscle fibre.
Press f and draw a freeform outline around another fibre; release to close it.
Press s (Selection mode) so no drawing tool is active, and click on empty background to deselect.
Capture the viewer area: both regions on the image and the two rows (class 'Region', Surface in px²) in the Region Editor.

shots.title: Wand region with its Sens. slider
steps: Open 'img01.png' and press w.
Click inside one muscle fibre; adjust 'Sens.' until the region fits the fibre.
Capture the viewer area including the Sens. slider.

shots.title: Brush with its Size slider
steps: Open 'img01.png' and click the Brush tool.
Set Size to about 60.
Paint a ring around one muscle fibre so the centre stays unpainted (a donut).
Capture the viewer area with the toolbar (Size slider visible).

shots.title: Region actions in the right-click menu, Simplify submenu open
steps: Draw two freeform regions on 'img01.png'.
Select both (s, click one, Shift-click the other).
Right-click on the image and hover 'Simplify'.
Capture with the menu and submenu open.

shots.title: Regions classified as Necrosis and Fibre, with the Classes panel
shots.capture: Viewer area including the Region Editor
steps: Open 'img01.png' and draw four regions (rectangle, freeform, wand, brush).
In the Region Editor set the first row's Class to 'Necrosis' from the dropdown.
Select the other three rows (click, then Ctrl/Cmd-click), click 'Edit class on selected rows' (tags icon), type 'Fibre' in '…or a new class' and press Enter.
Click on empty background to deselect.
Capture the viewer area: regions in their class colours and the Classes panel listing Necrosis and Fibre with their counts.

shots.title: Set class on the selected regions
steps: Select 2–3 rows in the Region Editor.
Click 'Edit class on selected rows' (tags icon).
Capture the Region Editor with the 'Set class on N selected region(s)' panel open.

shots.title: SAM box prompt: rectangles replaced by masks
shots.capture: Viewer area, before/after side by side
steps: Open 'img04.png'. Draw three rectangles (r) around three cells.
Capture (before). Click 'Segment' and wait for 'Added 3 region(s)'.
Capture (after) and place both side by side.

shots.title: SAM point prompt with an exclude point
steps: Click the SAM point prompts button.
Click one cell (include), then Shift-click a neighbouring area to exclude it.
Capture the preview region before pressing Enter.

shots.title: Segmentation tools and the SAM model picker
shots.capture: Toolbar crop with the open model menu
steps: Open 'img04.png'.
Click the chevron next to the Segment button.
Hover the ⓘ next to 'micro-sam ViT-B' so its info shows.
Capture the toolbar segmentation group with the menu and the info.

shots.title: Cellpose result: one region per cell
steps: Open '002_img.png' and draw one large rectangle over many cells.
Click 'Cellpose' (cells icon). The first run downloads the model (~588 MB).
When 'Added N cell region(s)' shows, capture the viewer area.

shots.title: The Region Editor listing regions from SAM and Cellpose
shots.capture: Viewer area including the Region Editor
steps: Open '002_img.png'.
Draw two rectangles around two single cells (r) and click 'Segment with SAM (box prompt)'; wait for 'Added 2 region(s)'.
Draw one rectangle over 15–30 other cells and click 'Segment cells (cellpose-SAM)'; wait for 'Added N cell region(s)'.
Open the Region Editor.
Capture the viewer area: the segmented outlines and the Region Editor whose Classes panel lists 'sam' and 'cell' with their counts.

shots.title: Spatial omics over the tissue image
shots.sample: spatial-omics → Adult mouse brain Visium H&E
steps: Open the 'spatial-omics' folder, click 'Adult mouse brain Visium H&E · 2,688 spots'.
Pick 'Spatial omics' in the plot-type dropdown.
Open the Spatial omics panel (toolbar button). Colour by → Group → cluster.
Capture the viewer area with the panel on the left.

shots.title: Gene map (expression field) under the spots
steps: Colour by → Gene → 'Ttr'.
Tick 'Gene map (expression field)', lower the markers' Opacity to 0.3.
Capture the viewer area.

shots.title: Select from ROIs: selected spots, the rest muted
steps: In the Visium H&E Spatial omics view, draw a freeform region (f) around one brain area.
Expand 'Regions' in the panel and click 'Select from ROIs'.
Capture: selected spots bright, others muted, hint 'n of N selected'.

shots.title: Counts per cluster with the selection overlaid
shots.sample: spatial-omics → Adult mouse brain Visium H&E
steps: Open the Visium H&E dataset and pick 'Spatial omics'; open the Spatial omics panel.
Colour by → Group → cluster.
Press f and draw a freeform region around the hippocampus.
Expand Regions and click 'Select from ROIs'.
Expand 'Distribution' (Counts is shown).
Capture the Distribution section: 'All' bars with the 'Selected' bars overlaid and the 'n selected' badge.

shots.title: Embedding (UMAP) with a lasso selection
steps: Open 'Mouse embryo seqFISH'. Colour by → Group → cell type column.
Distribution → Embedding (UMAP).
Lasso a cluster in the chart (lasso tool in the chart's modebar).
Capture the viewer area: the lassoed cells highlighted on the map and in the chart.

shots.title: An atlas region picked in the class tree and its cells selected in 3D
shots.sample: spatial-omics → Allen Brain Cell Atlas → Whole mouse brain MERFISH · 3D · 1-in-10
shots.capture: Viewer area with the Region Editor and the Spatial omics panel
steps: Open 'Whole mouse brain MERFISH · 3D · 1-in-10' and pick 'Spatial omics 3D'.

In the Region Editor click Import regions (upload icon) and select BOTH files at once: examples/brain-atlas/data/abc_atlas/image_volumes/MERFISH-C57BL6J-638850-CCF/20230630/resampled_annotation.nii.gz and examples/brain-atlas/data/ccf_2017_25um/ontology/structure_graph_1.json (from the brain-atlas download.sh; parts 'core' and 'merfish'). Wait for 'Regions imported'.
Open the Region Editor; in the class tree expand to a cortical area (e.g. Isocortex) and click it so the header shows 'name · title'.
Open the Spatial omics panel, expand Regions and click 'Select from ROIs'; wait for the hint 'n of N selected'.
Orbit so the selected cells are clearly visible against the muted ones.
Capture the viewer area showing the class tree with the pick, the hint in the Regions section and the selected cells.

shots.title: Spatial omics 3D: the whole-brain MERFISH atlas
steps: Open 'Whole mouse brain MERFISH · 3D · 1-in-10'.
Pick 'Spatial omics 3D'. Colour by → Group → a cell-class column.
Orbit so the brain is seen from above and the side; capture the viewer area.

shots.title: Multichannel fluorescence: per-channel colours and LUT row
steps: Open the WSI '2-channel fluorescence · 0.35 Gpx'.
Open Channels & Histogram, select the second channel, click 'Auto'.
Capture the viewer area with the dialog open (channel table with swatches, LUT row, histogram, sliders).

shots.title: A grayscale image with the Viridis colormap
steps: Open a micro-ct DCM slice.
In Channels & Histogram pick colormap 'Viridis' and click 'Auto'.
Close the dialog and capture the viewer area.

shots.title: Two intensity lines and the Intensity profile inset
steps: Open the WSI 'CMU-1' and zoom in on tissue.
Click 'Add an intensity line' twice.
Drag the endpoints of each line across a structure.
Capture the viewer area with both lines and the 'Intensity profile' inset.

shots.title: The toolbar detached as a floating window
steps: With 'img01.png' open, press and drag the ≡ handle at the left of the toolbar down into the image.
Release it so the toolbar floats over the image; the pin (Dock to top) button appears.
Capture the viewer area showing the floating toolbar over the image.

shots.title: A donut region and a Bézier region with handles
steps: Draw a brush ring (donut) and a polygon on 'img01.png'.
Select the polygon, right-click → Convert to Bézier.
Keep the Bézier region selected so its handles show; capture the viewer area.

shots.title: Dragging a selection box over several regions
steps: Open 'img01.png' and draw four small freeform regions (f) in a row.
Press s (Selection mode).
Press on empty background left of the regions and drag a box over three of them.
Capture while the mouse button is still held (use a delayed screenshot), showing the selection box over the regions.

shots.title: Manage annotation classes
steps: In the Region Editor, click 'Manage' (cog) in the Classes header.
Capture the whole dialog: class rows, fallback palette, auto-add checkbox, label matching, footer buttons.

shots.title: Classes panel above the region table
steps: With classified regions on an image, capture the 'Classes' panel of the Region Editor (search box, rows with eye, swatch, name, count, trash).

shots.title: The Region colour dialog
steps: Select regions of two different classes.
Click 'Edit colour of selected regions' (palette icon).
Capture the 'Region colour' dialog.

shots.title: Class tree of an atlas region set
steps: Open the 'spatial-omics' folder → Allen Brain Cell Atlas → 'Whole mouse brain MERFISH · 3D · 1-in-10'.
Open the Region Editor.

In the Region Editor click Import regions (upload icon) and select BOTH files at once: examples/brain-atlas/data/abc_atlas/image_volumes/MERFISH-C57BL6J-638850-CCF/20230630/resampled_annotation.nii.gz and examples/brain-atlas/data/ccf_2017_25um/ontology/structure_graph_1.json (from the brain-atlas download.sh; parts 'core' and 'merfish'). Wait for 'Regions imported'.
The Classes panel now shows the brain-region tree.
Expand two levels and click one class so it is picked (header shows 'name · title').
Capture the class tree.

shots.title: The Export Regions dialog
steps: In the Region Editor click 'Download regions as geojson file'.
Capture the 'Export Regions' dialog.

shots.title: The Save Mask dialog
steps: In the Region Editor click 'Download mask of the regions as PNG'.
Capture the dialog with the two mask-type options.

shots.title: The Slice slider for a z-stack in the Image view
steps: Click the TIFF 'GFPA_IBA1_AItestset_singletile_zstack_Series002.tif' and wait for decoding.
Move the Slice slider to the middle of the stack.
Capture the toolbar row with the Slice slider and its 'z of max' readout.

shots.title: Isosurface plot type with the Iso band slider
steps: With the micro-ct z-stack open, pick 'Isosurface'.
Move the 'Iso' band slider in the toolbar to about 80–255.
Capture the viewer area including the toolbar (Iso slider visible).

shots.title: Volume with axes and the Z-height grip
steps: In the Volume view, rotate so the top face of the box is visible.
Hover the round blue ↕ grip at the centre of the top face (its tooltip shows).
Capture the viewer area.

shots.title: Slice editor: 3D view, slice and X/Y sections
steps: In the Volume view, click the 'Slice editor' button.
Draw a freeform region (f) in the top-right slice pane.
Capture the 2×2 layout: 3D volume with the three planes, Z slice, X and Y sections.

shots.title: A class of regions shown as a 3D surface in the volume
shots.capture: Viewer area including the Region Editor
steps: Right-click a micro-ct slice to load the folder as a z-stack, pick 'Volume'.
Click 'Slice editor'. In the slice pane draw a freeform region (f) around the same structure on about 6 slices spread over the stack (move with the Slice slider between drawings).
Open the Region Editor, give these regions the class 'Tumor' (Edit class on selected rows).
Close the slice editor. In the Classes panel click the box icon 'Show in the volume, in 3D' next to 'Tumor'.
Rotate so the surface is visible inside the volume and capture the viewer area with the Region Editor.

shots.title: Show observations expressing with two picked genes
shots.sample: spatial-omics → Adult mouse brain Visium H&E
steps: Open the Visium H&E dataset in 'Spatial omics' and open the panel.
In 'Show observations expressing' pick 'Ttr' and 'Mbp'.
Choose 'Any gene'; leave 'Colour by these genes' ticked.
Capture the section: the picked-gene rows with their swatches, the Any/All switch, the checkbox and the hint.

shots.title: Observations in selection: counts per group
shots.sample: spatial-omics → Adult mouse brain Visium H&E
steps: Open the Visium H&E dataset in 'Spatial omics', open the panel, Colour by → Group → cluster.
Draw a freeform region over the cortex and click Regions → 'Select from ROIs'.
In Observations, expand 'Observations in selection'.
Capture the sub-section: label, observation and group counts, the bars per cluster and the copy button.

shots.title: Heatmap of picked genes per cluster
steps: Distribution → Heatmap; grouping 'cluster'.
Pick 5–8 genes in 'Pick genes for the rows' (e.g. Ttr, Mbp, Plp1, Nrgn, Hbb-bs).
Leave z-score on; capture the chart with the controls.

shots.title: The full toolbar in the Image view
steps: Click the sample 'img01.png'.
Make the browser wide enough that the toolbar fits on as few rows as possible.
Capture only the toolbar strip, from the drag handle (≡) to the Help (?) button.

shots.title: Plot-type dropdown open on a grayscale z-stack
shots.capture: Toolbar left part with the open dropdown
steps: Open the 'micro-ct' folder in the gallery.
Right-click any DCM slice to load the whole folder as a z-stack.
Click the plot-type dropdown (shows 'Image').
Capture the dropdown with its list open: Image, Heatmap, Contour, Surface, Volume, Isosurface.

shots.title: Contour plot type
steps: Open the 'micro-ct' folder and click one DCM slice (e.g. case1_040.dcm).
Pick 'Contour' in the plot-type dropdown.
Capture the viewer area.

shots.title: Surface plot type (3D height field)
steps: With a micro-ct slice open, pick 'Surface'.
Wait for the 3D surface to build (loading badge disappears).
Orbit a little (drag) so the relief is visible, then capture the viewer area.

shots.title: Zoom box being dragged
steps: Open the WSI 'CMU-1'.
Press b (or click the Zoom box button).
Press and drag a rectangle over the image and take the screenshot BEFORE releasing (outside is dimmed, box has white corners). Tip: use a delayed screenshot tool.

shots.title: Right-click menu on the image
steps: Open 'img01.png' and draw one rectangle (r, drag).
Select it (s, then click it).
Right-click on the image.
Capture the viewer area with the context menu open (region actions on top, then view and tool entries).

shots.title: Channels & Histogram on a grayscale image, colormap list open
shots.capture: The dialog with the colormap list open
steps: Open a micro-ct DCM slice.
Open Channels & Histogram.
Click the 'Colormap' selector and expand 'Perceptually Uniform Sequential'.
Capture the dialog with the colormap list open.

shots.title: 3D camera controls and resolution (toolbar)
steps: Load the micro-ct z-stack and pick 'Volume'.
Capture the toolbar: Zoom, Pan, Orbital, Turntable, Reset camera, 3D axes, Wireframe, Res dropdown, Slice editor.

shots.title: Region tools in the toolbar
steps: Open 'img01.png'.
Capture the part of the toolbar from the Region Editor button to the Delete (trash) button.

shots.title: Rectangle, polyline, freeform and polygon regions
steps: Open 'img01.png'.
Draw a rectangle (r), a polyline (l), a freeform region (f) and a polygon (Polygon tool, click vertices, click the first point to close).
Press s and click the polygon so its vertices show.
Capture the viewer area.

shots.title: Vertex eraser cursor over a region
steps: Draw a freeform region (f) on 'img01.png'.
Press e; set Radius to about 40.
Hover the circle cursor over the region's edge and capture before clicking.

shots.title: Before and after Merge / group
shots.capture: Two captures side by side, or one after-capture
steps: Draw two touching freeform regions; select both.
Capture (before), right-click → 'Merge / group', capture again (after: one region).
Place the two captures side by side in one image.

shots.title: Result of Inverse
steps: Draw two regions on 'img01.png' and select both.
Right-click → 'Inverse'.
Capture: the image rectangle selected, with the two regions as holes.

shots.title: The Simplify region(s) dialog
steps: Select a wand region (many vertices).
Right-click → Simplify → 'Custom…'.
Set the threshold to about 6 px and capture the dialog.

shots.title: The Region Editor
steps: Open the WSI 'CMU-1', draw 5–6 regions of different shapes.
Open the Region Editor; classify some as 'Tumor', 'Stroma', 'Necrosis'.
Select two rows (Ctrl-click).
Capture the whole Region Editor dialog: toolbar, Classes panel and table.

shots.title: The Region Editor toolbar
steps: With the Region Editor open and at least one region selected, capture only its toolbar (three rows of icons).

shots.title: Segmentation progress toast
steps: Clear the browser's site data (or use a private window) so the model is not cached.
Draw a rectangle on 'img04.png' and click Segment.
Capture the bottom-right 'SAM' toast while it shows the download progress bar.

shots.title: The Spatial omics panel
steps: Same setup as spatial-2d-overview.
Capture the full panel: header, Images, Observations (expanded), Regions, Distribution, Reset.

shots.title: Colour by Group: the Groups list
steps: Colour by → Group → cluster.
Untick two groups so they are hidden.
Capture the Colour by section with the Groups list.

shots.title: Colour by Gene with its key
steps: Colour by → Gene, search and pick 'Ttr' (or another strongly patterned gene).
Capture the viewer area with the panel: gene dropdown, key with colour bar, Colormap, Log scale and Clip outliers.

shots.title: Transcripts section (Xenium-type dataset)
shots.sample: A dataset with transcripts (e.g. a Xenium dataset in JIT) — not available on the demo server
steps: Open a dataset with transcripts (Xenium) in JIT.
Expand the Transcripts section, pick 3 genes, set 'View transcripts as' to Points.
Capture the Transcripts section.

shots.title: Counts chart
steps: Colour by → Group → cluster; expand 'Distribution'.
Capture the Counts chart.

shots.title: Histogram with a selection overlaid
steps: Colour by → Measurement → total_counts.
Select spots with 'Select from ROIs' (draw a region first).
Distribution → Histogram; capture (All and Selected overlaid).

shots.title: Violin split by cluster
steps: Colour by → Gene → 'Ttr'.
Distribution → Violin, grouping 'cluster'.
Capture the chart.

shots.title: A chart detached into its own window
steps: With any chart showing, click 'Detach'.
Move the chart window beside the map.
Capture the viewer area: panel says 'Shown in its own window.' and the chart window.
